title: Seamless chunk fallback and functioncall checkpointing
creator: Priya Singh
description: Implement a resilient server-sent events (SSE) streaming strategy that supports granular fallback of partial chunks, explicit functioncall checkpointing and rollback semantics, and graceful degradation for legacy clients. The goal is to minimize application-visible errors during short reconnects or partial payload losses while preserving functioncall atomicity and structured output parseability.
acceptance_criteria: Server exposes per-session chunk checkpoints that are inexpensive to create and resume from within a 60s reconnect window
Functioncall boundaries are checkpointed atomically so that retries do not result in duplicated tool invocations
Legacy clients that do not support checkpoints receive a compact retransmit protocol (token-window based) and a documented compatibility header
Reconnect flow preserves structured JSONL/NDJSON framing for consumers and avoids half-object emissions
End-to-end tests for reconnect + functioncall replay demonstrate no more than one duplicate invocation under intermittent reconnects in 1000 simulated sessions
progress_updates: 2026-02-22: Spike finished comparing three checkpoint formats: token-offset, chunk-UUID, and state-hash. Chose chunk-UUID with lightweight metadata to reduce coordination with runtime scheduler.

2026-02-27: Prototype server-side checkpoint API implemented (in-memory) and basic resume path working with websocket shim; initial perf shows <1ms checkpoint creation overhead for 99th percentile short responses.
2026-03-03: Integrated functioncall boundary metadata into checkpoint entries. Discovered a race condition when long-running tool calls are in-flight; added 'pending-call' flag to checkpoint record.
2026-03-07: Design review with PM and SDK leads. Agreed to add 'compat' request header for legacy clients and to provide a client library helper that can link checkpoints to user sessions.
2026-03-10: Began implementation of compact retransmit token-window and compatibility header. Implementing e2e tests and drafting docs for Console trace view integration.
decisions: Use chunk-UUID checkpoint format (UUID + sequence index + pending-call boolean) for resume semantics to avoid expensive token counting on resume path
Keep checkpoint lifetime short (configurable default 60s) to limit memory pressure on long-tail sessions and align with existing session lease heuristics (ENG-314159)

Provide explicit client compatibility header 'X-Redwood-Stream-V' to advertise support for checkpoints and compact retransmit; default server behavior will degrade to legacy token-window retransmit when header absent

Functioncall checkpoint semantics: do not mark checkpoint as 'complete' until tool invocation returns success/failure; allow idempotency keys to be passed through the functioncall wrapper for safe replays
tradeoffs: Chunk-UUID is simpler and cheaper than token-offset but requires deterministic chunk generation on producer and consumer to detect duplicates
Short checkpoint TTL reduces memory pressure but increases probability of non-resumable sessions for clients that reconnect slower than TTL
Adding pending-call flag increases checkpoint metadata size slightly but avoids duplicate tool invocation with complex rollback logic
Providing legacy token-window retransmit increases server-side bookkeeping for backward compatibility but keeps onboarding friction low for customers on older SDKs
implementation_notes: Server: extend stream session store with checkpoint index table (chunk_uuid -> offset metadata). Checkpoint creation is triggered at chunk boundaries and before functioncall frames.
SDK: add StreamSession.resume(checkpoint_id) helper that handles handshake and any retransmit negotiation; expose 'onCheckpoint' callback to apps for custom persistence
Protocol: new handshake fields: 'X-Redwood-Stream-V', 'Resume-Checkpoint', 'Resume-Window-Token' and response fields 'Resume-Accepted' and 'Resume-Offset'
Backpressure: when serving capacity constrained, prefer returning a small 'resumeable-ttl' header to clients instead of immediate disconnect to allow short reconnections
Observability: emit traces for checkpoint creation, resume attempts, replayed-functioncalls (with idempotency key) and failed resume reasons to Console (route-level dashboards)
qa_plan: Unit tests for checkpoint table operations (create/list/delete) and correct pending-call flag transitions
Integration test harness that simulates network flaps and asserts no more than one functioncall execution under reconnect scenarios
Chaos test on staging: random TCP kill, validate resume/compact retransmit works across kernel/quantized model variants
Compatibility tests: verify legacy header absent path falls back to token-window retransmit and that SDK helper correctly upgrades when 'X-Redwood-Stream-V' present
estimated_cost_savings: ~12% token cost reduction for long-lived interactive sessions due to fewer full-retransmits
notes: Follow-up: consider adding a small checkpoint compression format if metadata growth becomes an issue for high-concurrency tenants
Follow-up: coordinate with Console team to add checkpoint visualization per-route (trace view) so customers can see resume attempts
If rollout causes increased memory usage for multi-tenant noisy neighbors, add tenant-level checkpoint quotas
